subject: Clarify DPA & console copy: plain-language data flow + subprocessor listing
messages:
From: Elena Rios <elena.rios@acme.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: privacy@acme.com
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify DPA language and console copy for data flows

Hi Monica + Laura,

Thanks again for walking us through the hosted API controls last week. Legal ran a quick review and flagged two things we'd like help making customer-facing: 1) a short, plain-language line for the Console that explains where customer request data is processed and 2) a short explainer about how third-party subprocessors are listed and updated.

Our goals: the snippets should be simple enough for product teams to surface in the Console (100–200 characters for the status line and up to ~400 chars for a tooltip/learn-more). We also need an attachment or link for our procurement team that maps subprocessors to geography (we'll request that separately).

Could you send proposed lines and mark which ones are DPA/legal-approved vs product/backlog items? We also need to know whether the current DPA redlines you shared last week are considered final or still under discussion.

Attachments: none in this message.

—Elena
Elena Rios
Head of Procurement, Acme Software
elena.rios@acme.com

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Elena Rios <elena.rios@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA language and console copy for data flows

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Drafted two concise options below: one for the Console status line (short) and one for the tooltip/learn-more. I've also attached our working DPA redlines and a quick subprocessor snapshot CSV for procurement.

--- Proposed Console status line (choose one):
1) "Requests are processed in the region you choose; some infrastructure providers may route traffic for resilience."
2) "We process requests in your selected region; limited third-party infrastructure providers may handle temporary routing."

Recommended: option 1 (shorter + less legalese).

--- Proposed tooltip / learn-more (one paragraph, ~320 chars):
"When you send requests to Redwood's Hosted API, we process inputs and generate responses in the cloud region you select. For reliability and performance we use a handful of vetted infrastructure and networking providers; a current list of subprocessors and the geographic areas they operate in is linked below."

Notes on status vs. DPA: the wording above is intended for product UI copy. Karthik, can you confirm whether we can label the linked subprocessor list as 'current as of [date]' in the Console without implying contractual terms? Also, are there any mandated phrases from legal we must include (e.g., 'subprocessor' vs 'third-party processor')?

Files attached: Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx (internal redlines), subprocessor_map_snapshot.csv, console_snippets.txt

Next steps suggested:
- Legal to confirm preferred terminology and whether the 'current as of' language is acceptable (Karthik).
- Procurement (Acme) to confirm whether the CSV snapshot meets your mapping needs or if you need additional fields.
- Product to pick the final status line and schedule Console update (Queue: low priority, but we can accelerate).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

—Monica Patel
Senior Product Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, Elena Rios <elena.rios@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA language and console copy for data flows

Monica / Elena — quick editorial pass below; small suggestions in the tooltip for clarity.

Suggested tooltip revision (simpler):
"Redwood processes your requests in the cloud region you pick. To keep the service reliable we rely on a small set of vetted infrastructure and networking partners. See the linked list for the current subprocessors and the regions where they operate."

Rationale: replaces 'vetted infrastructure and networking providers' with 'partners' which reads friendlier in product contexts. Also suggests 'See the linked list' which is actionable.

I also added inline comments to Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx (minor phrasing tweaks).

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Developer Marketing (and occasional copy editor)
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Rios <elena.rios@acme.com>, privacy@acme.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 15:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA language and console copy for data flows

Thanks — short answers from Legal/Policy below.

1) Terminology: we prefer 'subprocessor' in contractual documents (DPA) and 'third-party partners' or simply 'partners' in product-facing UI. That aligns legal precision with customer-facing clarity.

2) "Current as of [date]" in the Console is okay for the linked list if the link goes to a managed doc (Drive or portal) that we can update; include a revision timestamp. Do not embed an oath of permanence in the UI copy.

3) DPA redlines: the copy in Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx is our current internal working draft (not yet signed). We're OK sending the redline to procurement for review, but mark it as draft and route signature questions through the Sales/Legal contact on this thread.

4) Product-safe short snippets (pick one set):
- Status line: "Requests are processed in the region you choose; third-party partners may assist with routing and reliability." (preferred legal/product compromise)
- Tooltip: "Redwood processes requests in your selected cloud region. We rely on a small set of vetted partners for hosting and networking; a live list of subprocessors and their operating regions is linked here (last updated: 2026-06-22)."

I've updated console_snippets.txt with these exact lines and added a version note.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
